changes.comment: Implement the atomic-write capability on the Node filesystem accessors (F2 of the filetree-atomic-write stream, completing the capability F1 declared). FsFileTreeAccessors now implements IAtomicFileTreeAccessors using a temporary/flush/rename/directory-flush protocol: an exclusively created private sibling temporary, the complete UTF-8 record written with short writes looped, an fsync and close of that temporary, a same-directory rename over the destination as the single visibility linearization point, and an fsync of the containing directory before success is reported. The destination is never unlinked, never truncated and never opened for writing; there is no copy fallback; a temporary is never promoted; and a completed replacement is never rolled back. Existing saveFileContents / saveFileBytes semantics are untouched - the atomic path is a sibling capability, not a replacement. Which guarantee a root may claim is decided per containing directory by positive identification against an allowlist: Linux with an ext2/ext3/ext4 or tmpfs filesystem advertises ['session', 'process-crash']; every other platform and filesystem, including any root whose filesystem cannot be identified, advertises no atomic replacement and refuses an atomic write rather than performing a weaker one. macOS is unqualified in this version because Node exposes no stable filesystem-type identifier on darwin, so a darwin root cannot be positively identified from inside this package. No 'os-crash' or 'power-loss' guarantee is advertised by anything. Failure classification is now exercised end to end: a failure at or before the rename reports the destination unchanged, a failure after it reports the replacement as visible, and a rename failure is only reported as having changed nothing when its errno is positive evidence that the kernel rejected it before touching a directory entry - ENOSPC, EDQUOT, EIO and an unrecognized or absent errno all classify as unknown. Adds cleanupAtomicTemporaries to IAtomicFileTreeAccessors and IAtomicFileTreeDirectoryItem (implemented on the filesystem, in-memory and DirectoryItem), which reclaims the working files an interrupted write leaves behind, at exclusive reopen, without handing consumers a naming convention to depend on. Removes 'cleanup' from IAtomicWriteFailure.stage: with the protocol implemented it has no producer, because a cleanup problem is reported in the failure message and never replaces the classification of the failure that caused it. Process-crash survival is evidenced by subprocess tests in which a child running the real protocol kills itself with SIGKILL at each protocol boundary, verified on ext4 and tmpfs; no OS-crash or power-loss claim follows from that evidence.
